Consider the set $A$ shown above. The interior of $A$ is 

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<x<1,\,\bbox[5px,border:1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196466/assets/19e8e52881066864cba562ed2a8cdc2944b9dae416c7124fdee207cdad1d8bdf.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196466/assets/907e996fb7aea36e0c924feb0f5d9dc6804c768be775953d277e84b0145ef5a0.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<x<1,\,-1<y<0\}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ge 4\}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅$

II. $A-∂A=\text{int}\,A$

III. $∂A⊂A$
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196466/assets/62c410c21e79e1bc688c1ff1a3440a207c62bcad42525bdc93fa2770b76d48bd.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196466/assets/33a4738b642443c2535d347aa53ee2b7b80c800142c4844d94578769118ebfbc.png)

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅,$ where $∅$ denotes the empty set.

- Statement II is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $A-∂A=\text{int}\,A.$

- Statement III is true. In this case, the set $A$ contains all of its boundary points, so we must have $∂A⊂A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+{y}^{2}<4\}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅$

II. $A-\text{int}\,A=∂A$

III. $∂A⊂{R}^{2}-A$
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196466/assets/4540e03fc5404474a0cd900c89004e6a5cfe7ac2d4702348e9d0395fc1c914e9.png)

 

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196466/assets/2a93b912f0d7b3a84bf0ec9c3b3596d080a9e71a345ff436e2f591edf042d9db.png)

  

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅,$ where $∅$ denotes the empty set.

- Statement II is false. Since $A$ contains none of its boundary points, we must have $A=\text{int}\,A$ or, equivalently,  $A-\text{int}\,A=∅.$

- Statement III is true. In this case, the set $A$ contains none of its boundary points, so we must have $∂A⊂{R}^{2}-A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and  III only."
